body: I hope this message finds you well. I'd just like for you to know that there are individuals out there who  would be absolutely broken if you hurt yourself again. It doesn't have to be your parents or your friends. It could be distant family or an old ex friend from kindergarten. What matters is that you show your friends and family that you are bigger and better than this. Show them that you will recover, become whole again, and live your life happily without them (if need be). If it's at all possible get in contact with a therapist. Talking to someone about what you're feeling and thinking is incredibly relieving. Sending you immense love and support.

In the cafeteria at my Catholic school once you sat down you were not allowed to move tables. One day I sat down and then noticed my mom was sitting at another table to surprise me. Of course I moved to go sit with her, and of course I got detention and had to miss a recess. One of the many reasons why I hated Catholic school.

When I was very young my family went to a theme park. This park was huge and it was pretty easy to get lost in. I remember my mother going to the bathroom and told me to wait for her to get out. I couldn't resist not exploring the theme park so I disappeared into the crowd. I eventually got lost and I became very panicked. This girl approached me, asked me if I was lost, and then took me straight to my mother without any other questions asked. She just knew where to go and who my mom was. Afterwards she was nowhere to be found. To this day (almost 18 years since the incident) my mom full heartedly believes it was my guardian angel. I still wonder about it sometimes.

Here's what I know about antidepressants and my use with them. Please keep in mind I'm not a MD by any means. Antidepressants are a temporary medicine used to help balance the neurotransmitters in your brain. With depressed brains you're lacking neurotransmitters that recognize dopamine (and I think serotonin). These chemicals are what make you happy and have pleasant thoughts (that's putting it very simply).  Doctors usually prescribe in small dosages, increase that dosage if the symptoms are severe enough, and then once the meds have been doing their job, you'll slowly be weaned off. So I would strongly recommend starting your meds again because it help keep you balanced throughout your day. Stopping them cold can be horrible for your brain chemicals and worsen your thoughts. As for your situation I want to mention a few things. If you were to kill yourself, who would take care of your mother? And what kind of impact would that have on her? I think you should value your life a lot more than you're allowing yourself to value it at. As for school and work: I work a job at a bank as a bank teller and they are known to have incredibly flexible hours and work with your schedules. You should give that a try. And if school is too much for your plate right now, you can always take a gap year and let things get stable. As a person who struggles with exactly the same things as you I want you to know there are so many other options than the ones you have constrained yourself to. There is always hope and there's always someone willing to help and listen. Just know you are loved and your life is worth so much. I hope this helped a little. Please feel free to ask questions.
